description: Figure 3d, labeled “AGNews clean-label,” displays the performance of different trigger word insertion positions—specifically “start,” “random,” and “end”—on the ASR (Automatic Speech Recognition) metric for the AGNews dataset under clean-label poisoning conditions, with a poisoning rate of 10% (2.5% of total samples). The horizontal axis lists the trigger words arranged in ascending order of their ASR values from the clean model, including “cf,” “bb,” “WNBA,” “ESPN,” “NHL,” “FIFA,” “Estadio,” and “athletics.” The vertical axis represents ASR values, ranging from 0.5 to 0.9, with tick marks at regular intervals. The “start” position is shown as a green line with circle markers, the “random” position as an orange line with cross markers, and the “end” position as a purple line with diamond markers. Across the x-axis, all three lines exhibit fluctuations but generally trend upward, with the “start” line starting at approximately 0.78 and ending near 0.90, the “random” line beginning at around 0.65 and concluding near 0.85, and the “end” line initiating at about 0.75 and finishing near 0.80. Notably, the “start” line reaches its peak at “FIFA” with an ASR of approximately 0.92, while the “end” line dips to its lowest point at “bb” with an ASR of approximately 0.58.
